decisions.reason: As a standard rye bread in a German bakery assortment, it likely supports the core range and is unlikely to be withdrawn so soon after launch.
The premium raisin stollen has an explicitly stated gold-medal result, making it a strong seasonal flagship that management would almost certainly retain.
A rye mixed bread with seeds fits stable mainstream demand in Germany and is likely to remain part of the regular bread lineup.
This darker malted rye variant is somewhat more niche in taste but still fits the firm's bread competence, so it is more likely to be kept than dropped.
Marzipan stollen is a plausible seasonal extension alongside the award-winning raisin version and would usually be kept unless sales clearly disappoint.
The ancient grain bread was presented as the firm's newest 'Meisterstück' and matches premium natural-grain trends, so management would likely continue it while monitoring demand.
